key_insight: The paper shows that fine-tuning vision-language-action (VLA) policies with only episode-level success/failure signals works better when the signal is decomposed hierarchically, instead of collapsing everything into one scalar reward. This gives the actor more targeted guidance at the transition level, especially once the task is already partly solvable.
problem_solved: Online RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLAs often receives only a single binary outcome per episode, but policy updates need per-step supervision. A single scalar advantage can blur different types of feedback and becomes less informative after basic success is achieved.
method: Introduces hierarchical advantage weighting to convert sparse episode outcomes into more structured transition-level training signals.
Separates different feedback roles instead of using one flat reward/advantage, helping the actor learn which transitions mattered within a rollout.
Improves fine-tuning under sparse binary outcomes by providing more informative supervision for online RL on pretrained VLA policies.
impact: For practitioners, this offers a more effective way to fine-tune robot and multimodal policies when dense rewards are unavailable. It can improve learning stability and sample efficiency in real-world settings where only success/failure labels are easy to obtain.

paper_title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes
paper_authors: Tongyan Fang, Siyuan Huang, Naiyu Fang, Ganlong Zhao, Zhongjin Luo
